instructions: Up to 3 days ahead: in a large bowl, stir together the lukewarm water, yeast, sugar, salt and olive oil.

Add the flour 1 cup at a time, stirring with a wooden spoon until the dough is too stiff to stir. Transfer it to a lightly floured counter and knead for 8 minutes, until it's soft and no longer sticks to your hands.
Put the dough back in the bowl, cover it with a clean towel and leave it for 1 hour, until it's puffy.
Fold the edges of the dough into the middle to push out the air. Cut it into 8 equal pieces, roll each into a ball and cover them with the towel.
On a lightly floured counter, roll each ball into a round about 6 inches across and 1/4 inch thick.

Heat a large dry skillet over medium heat. Put in 1 round and cook until the edges puff up, about 1 minute. Flip it and cook until the other edges puff. Keep flipping 3 more times, about 4 minutes in all, until the flatbread puffs up and has golden spots. Stack the finished flatbreads in a towel and cook the rest the same way.
Let the flatbreads cool completely. Wrap the flatbreads in a towel and keep them in a zip bag in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze them with a sheet of parchment between each for up to 3 months.
To serve, warm each flatbread in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds on each side, or 1 minute on each side if frozen. Serve warm with butter or white cheese.
advance_prep_notes: make a batch up to 3 days ahead; keeps in the fridge or freezes
method_notes: Yemek.com's bazlama (4.4 from 22 ratings) is a yeasted dough of flour, water, olive oil, sugar and salt, rolled thin and flipped several times in a dry pan until it puffs. Roaming Taste and Yemek.com's pan version add yogurt for a softer bread; the lead has none, so this keeps to the lead and halves its flour. Sources agree the cooked breads freeze well. The fridge time of 3 days is a normal range for yeast flatbreads and was not stated by the sources. The dough needs a 1 hour rise, which is hands off.
